children: Maple Leaf Foods plans to consolidate its U.S. plant protein production into a single site in Indianapolis.
The consolidation will include winding down production at plants in Seattle and Turners Falls, Mass., the Canadian consumer packaged goods company said.

Maple Leaf plans to execute the transition over about 12 to 18 months, with targeted completion in the fourth quarter of 2027. Production will continue in Seattle and Turners Falls during the transition period.
The company plans to invest in the Indianapolis facility and add employees there to expand the scope of operations. Maple Leaf didn't say how many employees would be affected.

The consolidation follows a review of Maple Leaf's plant-protein manufacturing footprint and is intended to make the network more efficient. It is part of Maple Leaf's broader initiative to simplify operations and improve the competitiveness of its manufacturing network.
The expected benefits and costs of the move are disclosed in Maple Leaf's previously disclosed 2030 financial outlook.
